findings.title: Documentation dividers bypass the quiet-border token
findings.summary: The shared documentation shell defines #CECECE but later uses the older #B1B4B6 for contents, history, example frames, catalogues and mobile section dividers. This is a confirmed token inconsistency, not a claim that every grey border fails contrast.

evidence.detail: Contents navigation uses an independent structural grey.
Example frames use the same older hardcoded grey.

findings.proposed_change: Resolve decorative separators through the shared quiet-border role and remove superseded declarations. Keep inputs, active tabs and focus indicators on their stronger, separately tested roles.
acceptance: Computed decorative borders use #CECECE in the light documentation theme.
Inputs and focus remain visually distinguishable; keyboard and narrow-layout checks pass.
Review adjacent sections together at desktop and phone widths.
findings.review_scope: Static source review; proposed remediation, no runtime change in this package.

findings.title: Small-screen examples contradict the documented body-text scale
findings.summary: The example stylesheet explicitly reduces body text to 16px below 500px and imports the GOV.UK responsive type defaults. The local typography contract specifies 18–19px narrow-screen body text and 19px for maintained custom main controls; the reference examples do not state this extra density exception.

evidence.detail: Example body text is explicitly 16px on narrow screens.
The published narrow-screen starting point is 18px to 19px.

findings.proposed_change: Choose one explicit responsive type contract for reference examples and maintained controls, then configure the imported typography and custom styles together. Preserve the separately documented native HA and chart-label density exceptions.
acceptance: Compare computed paragraph, input, button and help-text sizes with their documented roles at 320px and desktop.
Reflow and 200% text resizing retain complete names, units and errors.
Examples and copied markup demonstrate the same declared scale.
findings.review_scope: Static source review; proposed remediation, no runtime change in this package.

findings.title: Custom examples retain a second set of semantic colours
findings.summary: The custom status and do/don’t-list styles still use #00703C and #D4351C while the maintained semantic references use #0F7A52 and #CA3535. Several old declarations remain alongside later corrective overrides. Reference controls can therefore demonstrate a competing palette despite passing basic contrast checks.

evidence.detail: Custom list symbols use the older green/red pair.

findings.proposed_change: Create one documentation semantic-token mapping from the local contract, apply it to custom status/list components and configure upstream component variables where appropriate. Remove obsolete duplicate rules without erasing intentional functional exceptions.
acceptance: Reference success/error components resolve to the declared local roles.
Text, fills and on-fill colours pass their actual context checks.
The MOJ badge keeps its correct rounded shape and fixed attention role; no global recolouring is introduced.
findings.review_scope: Static source review; proposed remediation, no runtime change in this package.

findings.title: Lighting summaries can conceal partially unavailable rooms
findings.summary: The lighting card calculates its denominator from available lights, then labels it simply “lights”. A room with two available lights off and a third unavailable light can read “2 of 2 lights off”, omitting the unavailable member from the visible summary. The same omission can affect an unknown managed member; the capability model records unknown and unavailable separately.

evidence.detail: The count uses availableLights without qualifying the visible denominator.
Any available member selects that count instead of an unavailable explanation.

findings.proposed_change: Describe available-state counts, unavailable and unknown managed members separately. Preserve reserved-light exclusions and user room names. Do not infer that an unavailable or unknown member is off.
acceptance: A fixture with two off members and one unavailable member exposes both facts in the visible and accessible summary.
All-off, mixed-on, unknown, partially unavailable, fully unavailable and empty rooms remain distinct.
Reserved or out-of-scope lights remain excluded from control actions.
findings.review_scope: Static source review; proposed remediation, no runtime change in this package.

findings.title: Per-room lighting requests lack a pending explanation
findings.summary: Bulk lighting actions track an in-flight request, but individual room turn-on/stop actions await the service call without a pending message. The control continues to show the previous action while the request is unresolved. No false success claim is made, but uncertainty is not explained.

evidence.detail: Per-room turn-on awaits a request with only a failure branch.
Per-room stop likewise has no pending feedback.
Only the bulk path tracks actionPending.

findings.proposed_change: Define a shared per-room request state with sending, accepted, confirmed or unconfirmed wording. Prevent unintended duplicate submissions while preserving a clear recovery route; do not turn an accepted service call into physical confirmation.
acceptance: Delayed, rejected and accepted-but-unconfirmed requests have distinct observable copy.
Repeated activation cannot queue accidental duplicate commands while a request is pending.
Native reported state remains separate and cancellation does not claim to undo a sent action.
findings.review_scope: Static source review; proposed remediation, no runtime change in this package.

findings.title: The search catalogue omits section and publishing hubs
findings.summary: Search is presented as a complete catalogue, but it reuses section navigation groups that exclude index pages. The new writing hub has an explicit exception, while other section and publishing hubs remain absent from searchable results.

evidence.detail: Section-group filtering omits index routes except the new writing hub.
Global search reuses the filtered groups.
The no-JavaScript explanation promises a complete catalogue.

findings.proposed_change: Give search its own complete editorial catalogue, retaining section/group metadata for organisation. Keep sidebar filtering separate. Include hubs and meaningful entry pages without recursive links to the search page itself.
acceptance: Search by the exact title of each editorial hub finds its canonical route.
The no-JavaScript list contains the same intended searchable pages.
Navigation grouping and current-page state remain unchanged.
findings.review_scope: Static source review; proposed remediation, no runtime change in this package.

findings.title: The dense-chart deviation is outside its table structure
findings.summary: A blank line separates CIV-016 from the deviation table. It renders as a paragraph containing pipe characters, so the chart-colour and 1.5px-line decision loses the table’s header associations and is harder to read.

evidence.detail: This row is separated from the preceding Markdown table by a blank line.

findings.proposed_change: Restore CIV-016 to the semantic deviation table. Keep its exact chart-colour and line-weight decision intact.
acceptance: The built HTML contains CIV-016 in a table row with the same headers as the other decisions.
No raw table pipe syntax is exposed in reading text.
Keyboard scrolling and narrow-layout checks still pass.
findings.review_scope: Static source review; proposed remediation, no runtime change in this package.

migration_recommendations.title: Existing promotional illustrations need the new illustration treatment
migration_recommendations.summary: The existing decorative homepage hero predates the new illustration family and uses ornamental outlines and several supporting colours. Its empty alternative is appropriate in the decorative homepage placement. The new-asset rules do not retrospectively establish a MUST violation; migration is recommended for visual consistency when the artwork is next revised.

evidence.detail: The decorative laptop, panel and approval motif use repeated outlines and multiple supporting colours.
Attribution is collective rather than a per-asset delivery record.

migration_recommendations.proposed_change: Redraw or simplify the decorative hero and category compositions using the declared flat illustration family. Record each original asset’s purpose, creator/rights, intended backgrounds and alternative-text decision. Preserve supplied identity artwork and meaningful functional symbols.
acceptance: The hero has a clear focal point and restrained supporting colours without ornamental outlining.
Each decorative asset has a traceable metadata record and justified empty or informative alternative.
Inspect actual mobile/desktop placement; functional chart and icon stroke requirements remain unchanged.
